summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease post-kidney transplant, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and pulmonary hypertension was admitted for acute dyspnea and cough. Evaluation revealed volume overload with elevated BNP (5376), bilateral pleural effusions, and moderate pulmonary hypertension on echocardiogram, consistent with acute on chronic heart failure. He was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned to increased oral torsemide (100 mg BID). Symptoms improved, and he was euvolemic at discharge with a weight of 155.7 lbs. The pericardial effusion remained stable without tamponade. He was discharged home on optimized diuretic therapy with plans for outpatient follow-up, CT chest for restrictive lung evaluation, and monitoring of renal function and tacrolimus levels.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
End stage renal disease status post kidney transplant
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
